goals: A minimal Expo template for English-only iOS and Android MVPs that AI coding agents extend safely.
Production-ready auth on two variant branches (Supabase and Firebase): Google sign-in on both platforms, Sign in with Apple on iOS.
One brand look with platform-correct behaviour on iOS and Android.
Anything that can be checked by a script is checked by a script; only judgement stays as prose.
Works from Windows, Linux and macOS, with bun only and TypeScript only.
Production bar: a change is done when the local checks pass, both platforms were exercised, and nothing is called working from reading code alone.
nonGoals: A profiles table or any user data model
A third auth provider as a branch

core.typescript-only.rule: Source, scripts, hooks and configs are TypeScript. The only .js files are `jest.config.js` (Jest 29 loads a TypeScript config through ts-node, which is not a dependency, and that fails under verbatimModuleSyntax) and `metro.config.js` (Metro loads its config through Node, which reads TypeScript only from version 22.18 on while engines allows 22.12, and it cannot resolve expo/metro-config from an ES module). No .mjs, .cjs, .jsx or .sh files.
core.typescript-only.why: One language for the app, the tooling and the agents; Windows-safe; type-checked.

core.no-server-code.rule: The template ships no server code: no Edge Functions, Cloud Functions or backend services.
core.no-server-code.why: A template with a server forces every app onto one backend and one deployment story. Server pieces ship as pattern docs.

core.public-env-only.rule: Only publishable values go under EXPO_PUBLIC_*; anything else is a secret and never enters the JS bundle.
core.public-env-only.why: EXPO_PUBLIC_* values are inlined into the bundle and readable in both the iOS and the Android binary.

core.no-real-config.rule: Only example env and config files are committed; real config is gitignored and lives locally or in EAS.
core.no-real-config.why: Committed Firebase, Google or Supabase config leaks project identifiers and invites committed secrets. Each app and each environment has its own values. No script can tell a real config file from an example, so the reviewer of every diff checks it; secrets:check only catches key formats with a known prefix.

core.tokens-in-keychain.rule: Tokens and credentials are kept in expo-secure-store, or in storage encrypted with a key that lives there; never in plain MMKV, AsyncStorage or logs.
core.tokens-in-keychain.why: Plain app storage is readable from device backups and on rooted devices; Keychain and Keystore are hardware-backed where the device has it.

core.pattern-not-code.rule: Optional features ship as pattern docs, not as code in the template.
core.pattern-not-code.why: Core stays minimal and every line in it is tested. A pattern is applied only when an app picks it.

core.minimal-abstraction.rule: Write the simplest code that works: no new layer, wrapper, option or abstraction until a second real use needs it.
core.minimal-abstraction.why: Agents over-build. Every abstraction is code to review, test and keep, so delete before adding.

intake.audit-record.rule: No dependency is added without an approved intake record covering licence, maintenance, adoption, source read, provenance, Expo SDK and New Architecture compatibility, native impact and migration cost.
intake.audit-record.why: A dependency is code we ship and cannot read in full. The record makes the choice reviewable, and a human approves it before anything is installed.

intake.pin-risky-native.rule: A native package with a bus factor of one, or a version below 1.0, is pinned to an exact version.
intake.pin-risky-native.why: A native module breaks the build, not just the app. A caret range lets an unreviewed release in.

backport.criteria.rule: A feature backported from a production app must be generic, tested and inside the template's scope.
backport.criteria.why: The template stays reusable and minimal. App-specific code does not belong in it, and a human decides what is generic.

auth.nonce.rule: Every ID-token sign-in uses a fresh nonce: the hashed nonce goes to the identity provider, the raw nonce to the backend, and a cached token is never sent to a backend.
auth.nonce.why: A cached token carries no fresh nonce, so a replayed token would pass the backend check.

auth.apple-with-google.rule: Where Google sign-in is offered on iOS, Sign in with Apple is offered too.
auth.apple-with-google.why: App Store guideline 4.8 requires an equivalent privacy-focused login next to any third-party login.

release.r8-e2e.rule: After a native change, re-run the Android release (R8) e2e before shipping.
release.r8-e2e.why: R8 minification can strip or rename classes that a debug build keeps, and only a release build shows it.
